data.name: Ayyam
data.gender_notes: Ayyam is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Refers to the five daily prayers in Islam. The name Ayyam carries the meaning “Days” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ayyam usually hope their child will grow to embody days and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a commitment to daily spiritual practice.
data.etymology: Ayyam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Days.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayyam total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: أَيّام
in_arabic.meaning: أَيّام أَسماء سَمَّيت بِها أَيّام اللہ
in_arabic.long_meaning: أَيّام هي أَيّام اللہ المُقَدَّسة في الہِدايَة، وَهِيَ الأَيّام الَّتِي تُصَنَّفُها اللہ بِحُسنِهِ وَرِضاهُ، فَكُلٌّ مِن هَذِهِ الأَيّام مُحَيَّرَة بِطَولِهَا وَبِقُدْرَتِهَا، وَهِيَ الأَيّام الَّتِي تُجَمِعُ اللہ فِيهَا خَلائِقَهُ وَقَومَهُ، وَتُؤَخِّذُهُم بِحَسَبِ إِقبالِهِم عَلى الدِينِ وَالسّلوكِ الصالحِ

in_urdu.name: ایّام
in_urdu.meaning: ایّام اللہ کی ایک قسم کے نام سے دیتے ہیں
in_urdu.long_meaning: ایّام اللہ ہدایت میں ایک مقدس دن کے لیے ہوتے ہیں، اللہ تعالیٰ نے ان دنوں کو اپنی رحمت اور فضل کے مطابق طے کیا ہے، ان دنوں میں اللہ تعالیٰ اپنے مخلوقات کو جمع کرتا ہے اور انہیں ان کے اعمال کے مطابق جزا دیتا ہے، ایک ایک دن ایسا ہے جس میں اللہ تعالیٰ کے فضل و کرم سے اللہ کے بندوں کے حالات بدلتے ہیں

in_hindi.name: ऐयाम
in_hindi.meaning: ऐयाम भी अल्लाह के नामों में से एक है
in_hindi.long_meaning: ऐयाम अल्लाह के नामों में से एक है जो अल्लाह के दिनों को दर्शाता है, जिन्हें अल्लाह ने अपनी मर्जी के अनुसार निर्धारित किया है, जिनमें अल्लाह के बन्दे को अपने कर्मों के अनुसार सزا देता है, यह अल्लाह का एक अद्वितीय दिन है जिसमें अल्लाह के बन्दे के حالात बदलते हैं

in_english.name: Ayyam
in_english.meaning: Ayyam is a name of some days of Allah
in_english.long_meaning: Ayyam is a name of some days of Allah, which are considered sacred in religion. Allah has chosen these days by His grace and mercy. On these days, Allah gathers His creatures and rewards them according to their deeds. It is a day of favor and blessing from Allah, where He changes the circumstances of His servants

data.cultural_impact: The term "Ayyam" in Islamic culture signifies the five daily prayers that are required for every practicing Muslim. Each prayer speaks to a particular time of day and acknowledges the divine presence and power that is omnipresent. The communal nature of performing these prayers in the mosque (Masjid) strengthens the bonds between the Muslim community and reinforces their shared religious and cultural identity.
data.spiritual_significance: The regular observance of the five daily prayers holds profound spiritual significance for Muslims. These prayers act as a means to purify the soul, seek divine guidance, and strengthen the spiritual bond between the individual and their Creator. Through these prayers, Muslims also ask for forgiveness for their sins, seek blessings for themselves and their loved ones, and express gratitude for the countless blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them. The spiritual discipline and devotion instilled by this practice ultimately fosters inner peace, contentment, and a closer relationship with God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Days" symbolizes Refers to the five daily prayers in Islam.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ayyam serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of days.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The period of Ayyam al-Jihad, or 'Days of Struggle', marked a turning point in the Third Islamic Civil War (652-661 AD) during which Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth rightly-guided caliph, faced numerous rebellions from various factions within the Islamic community. During this time, Ali successfully defended his territories against the invasion of the Byzantine and Sasanian armies, securing his position as caliph.

The term 'Ayyam al-Arba'ah', or 'Four Days', refers to a critical period in the early Islamic history when the Prophet Muhammad, in Medina, was besieged by the Meccan army during the Battle of the Trench (627 AD). During this time, the Muslims managed to hold off the enemy’s attacks for four consecutive days, which proved to be a turning point in the battle and a significant victory for the Muslims.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Ayyam' in Islamic context refers to the annual observance of the Prophet Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina, known as the 'Hijra'. This event is commemorated as 'Ayyam al-Hijra' or 'Mawlid al-Nabawi' and is celebrated globally by Muslims. On social media platforms like Twitter, Instagram, and YouTube, this occasion is marked with special hashtags, visual content, and educational videos. Users share their personal reflections and experiences, as well as historical facts and insights into Islamic culture. The trending topics often revolve around Islamic holiday, Middle Eastern culture, and spiritual growth. #AyyamAlHijra #IslamicCelebrations #SpiritualGrowth
